newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA chief hints at crude overproduction.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA chief hints at crude overproduction.

text.p: Revenue estimates given by Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA President Luis Giusti Thursday suggest that the country is producing well over its OPEC quota and exporting an average of 2.739 million barrels per day (bpd).

"If the average price (for Venezuela's basket of crude and products) ends the year at $15.60 (per barrel) we would be talking about revenues of at least $15.6 billion," Giusti told reporters before addressing a Seminar.
Using Giusti's figures, it appears that PDVSA expects to export about 1 billion barrels of crude and products in 1996, giving a daily average of 2.739 bpd.
"If the price ends at $16.50 (per barrel), as is probable..., we would then be taking about (revenues of) $16.5 billion," Giusti added.
Giusti was careful not to place an exact figure on Venezuela's crude exports or production.
Venezuelan oil officials regularly reject accusations that Venezuela consitently flouts its OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd.
According to a Reuters survey, Venezuela pumped 3.12 million bpd in August.
According to PDVSA figures the domestic market accounted for 378,000 bpd in 1995.
